                    ### Question
                    A study is being conducted in a health center to determine the effect of exposure to tobacco smoke in children of smoking parents. For this purpose, a group of healthy children between 3 and 7 years old whose parents are smokers is selected and at the same time an equal number of children whose parents are non-smokers are selected in the same center. A year later, the appearance of respiratory diseases during that year will be investigated in both groups. Indicate the correct answer:

                    ### Options
                    opa. The study design is a prospective cohort.
opb. The study design is cases and controls.
opc. The study design follows a qualitative methodology.
opd. The study is experimental.
ope. The type of design used is efficient to study rare diseases.

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The study design is a prospective cohort study. It involves selecting a group of healthy children with smoking parents and a comparable group with non-smoking parents, followed by a one-year follow-up to investigate the incidence of respiratory diseases. This design allows for the observation of outcomes over time without random assignment, confirming it is not experimental. Additionally, there are no defined cases and controls, ruling out a case-control study design. The study is not qualitative as it focuses on quantitative outcomes (respiratory diseases) rather than qualitative data. Lastly, the design is not efficient for studying rare diseases, as it targets a common outcome (respiratory diseases) rather than rare conditions. Therefore, the correct answer is that the study design is a prospective cohort.
